entity_types.name: ThreatActor
entity_types.label: Threat actor
entity_types.description: An individual attacker, persona or unnamed actor (e.g. 'a Russian-speaking hacker', 'the operator'). Named APT groups are ThreatGroup.

entity_types.name: ThreatGroup
entity_types.label: Threat group
entity_types.description: A named hacking group, APT or crime gang (APT28, Lazarus Group, FIN7, OilRig).

entity_types.name: Malware
entity_types.label: Malware
entity_types.description: Malicious software: backdoors, RATs, trojans, ransomware, loaders (X-Agent, PlugX, WannaCry, Emotet).

entity_types.name: AttackTechnique
entity_types.label: Attack technique
entity_types.description: A specific adversary technique, usually a MITRE ATT&CK technique or ID (Spearphishing Attachment, T1566.001, credential dumping).

entity_types.name: Vulnerability
entity_types.label: Vulnerability
entity_types.description: A software weakness or exploit, including CVE IDs (CVE-2017-11882, a zero-day in Flash, EternalBlue).

entity_types.name: Software
entity_types.label: Software
entity_types.description: Legitimate software or a product that is attacked, abused or vulnerable (Microsoft Office, Windows, Adobe Flash).

entity_types.name: Tool
entity_types.label: Tool
entity_types.description: Dual-use or offensive tooling that is not malware itself (Mimikatz, PsExec, Impacket, PowerShell).

entity_types.name: Organization
entity_types.label: Organization
entity_types.description: A targeted or involved company, agency or sector (banks, government agencies, Microsoft, the energy sector).

entity_types.name: AttackPattern
entity_types.label: Attack pattern
entity_types.description: A general method or style of attack not tied to one technique (phishing, watering hole attacks, supply-chain attack, brute force).

entity_types.name: FileHash
entity_types.label: File/hash
entity_types.description: A file name, file sample or hash (MD5/SHA1/SHA256) (invoice.doc, svchost.exe, d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e).

entity_types.name: NetworkInfra
entity_types.label: Network infrastructure
entity_types.description: An IP address, domain, URL or server used in attacks, including defanged forms (185.12.45[.]6, evil[.]com, C2 server).

entity_types.name: Asset
entity_types.label: Asset/system
entity_types.description: A victim system, device or network (email servers, ICS systems, endpoints, domain controllers).

entity_types.name: SecurityTeam
entity_types.label: Security team
entity_types.description: A security vendor, research team or CERT (FireEye, Kaspersky Lab, Unit 42, US-CERT).

entity_types.name: Time
entity_types.label: Time
entity_types.description: A date, year, month or period (2017, March 2019, late 2018).

entity_types.name: Location
entity_types.label: Location
entity_types.description: A country, region, city or nationality (Russia, the Middle East, Ukrainian).

relations.name: alias-of
relations.description: two names for the same actor or group

relations.name: uses
relations.description: an actor, group, technique or pattern uses malware, a tool, software, a technique or a pattern

relations.name: targets
relations.description: an actor, group or technique targets an organization, asset or vulnerability

relations.name: operates-in
relations.description: an actor or group is active in a location

relations.name: originated-from
relations.description: an actor or group comes from a location

relations.name: active-at
relations.description: an actor or group is active at a time

relations.name: variant-of
relations.description: malware, a tool or a pattern is a variant of another

relations.name: sub-technique-of
relations.description: a technique is a sub-technique of another

relations.name: drops
relations.description: malware drops a file

relations.name: exploits
relations.description: malware or a tool exploits a vulnerability

relations.name: affects
relations.description: malware or a vulnerability affects software or an asset

relations.name: communicates-with
relations.description: malware or a tool communicates with network infrastructure

relations.name: contains
relations.description: software contains a vulnerability

relations.name: runs-on
relations.description: software runs on an asset/system

relations.name: remediated-by
relations.description: a vulnerability is remediated by a software patch

relations.name: belongs-to
relations.description: infrastructure or an asset belongs to an organization

relations.name: located-in
relations.description: something is located in a location (generic: only when no specific relation fits)

relations.name: monitored-by
relations.description: an asset/system is monitored by a security team

relations.name: indicates
relations.description: a file/hash indicates malware or a threat actor

relations.name: downloads-from
relations.description: a file downloads from network infrastructure

relations.name: utilized-by
relations.description: network infrastructure is utilized by an actor, group or malware

relations.name: investigates
relations.description: a security team investigates an actor or group

relations.name: detects
relations.description: a security team detects malware, a vulnerability or an attack pattern

relations.name: mitigates
relations.description: a security team mitigates a technique or vulnerability

relations.name: patches
relations.description: a security team patches an asset/system

relations.name: occurs-at
relations.description: something happens at a time (generic: only when no specific relation fits)

assumptions.note: Threat group uses Software is missing from the PDF (Threat actor has it); assumed an omission.
The PDF only has actor<->group aliases; ATT&CK aliases are group<->group (APT28 = Fancy Bear).

notes: The PDF's '4 mitigated-by 13' and '13 mitigates 5' are one family, stored as 'mitigates' (13 -> 4, 13 -> 5).
The PDF spells 'sub_technique_of'; it is written 'sub-technique-of' to match the other names.
Entity groups and descriptions are not in the PDF; they are ours, for the UI and the LLM prompt.
